releases.name: huggingface/transformers
releases.body_excerpt:
# Release v5.23.0


## New Model additions

### Inkling2



Inkling 2 Small is a multimodal model from Thinking Machines Lab that accepts text and image inputs and generates text outputs, and it is intended for use in English and other languages and across multiple coding languages. Its language backbone has 48 mixture-of-experts decoder layers, each routing tokens to 8 of 384 experts, for 594B total and 17B active parameters. It keeps the Inkling decoder (learned relative attention, short causal convolutions, mixture-of-experts layers) and adds block attention residuals, gated attention with a learned sink, and dynamic key/value convolutions. Images are encoded by a Perception Encoder-based vision transformer and projected into the language model embeddings, one embedding per 40x40 pixel patch.

**Links:** Documentation | Blog Post
* Add inkling2 (#50682) by @guarin in #50682

### JEV

JEV is a decision head that scores single-token labels with a linear layer at the last token of the prompt, soft-capped like the logits of a language model head. `JevForDecision` is the model of the checkpoint and its head, and it reads the head files shipped next to the weights (`head.safetensors` and `judge_config.json` for JEV). The same head is also used by GEV and reads the 255 answer codes of pplx-decider and d3, and it can be run through the experimental `decision` pipeline or directly with `decide`.

**Note:** JEV and the decision pipeline are currently experimental. Their APIs, configuration, and behavior may change as development continues. They should be used with caution in production environments.

**Links:** Documentation
* Add Jev + decision core (#50054) by @ArthurZucker in #50054

### LFM3



LFM3 is the third generation of Liquid Foundation Models from Liquid AI. Like LFM2, it is a hybrid architecture that combines gated short convolutions with grouped-query attention, with the attention layers split between full-attention and sliding-wind

## New Models

### Mistral Large 4 (Le Chonk)



Mistral Large 4 is Mistral's largest and most capable model to date: a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal Mixture-of-Experts model with 49 billion active parameters per token (52 billion including embeddings and output layers), trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's own datacenters in Europe.

Mistral Large 4 unifies instruction following, reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows in a single set of weights. While a generalist model, it shows especially good performance on workloads such as cybersecurity, finance, and law, and it surpasses frontier closed models on visual grounding. It is natively fluent in 160+ languages, including every official language of the European Union.

#### Key Features

Mistral Large 4 includes the following architectural choices:

- **~1T total / ~52B active parameters**: granular Mixture-of-Experts with 128 routed experts (4 active per token) and 1 shared expert.
- **1M context length**, for long-context workloads.
- **Multimodal input**: accepts text and image input, with text output. Pixtral-style vision encoder trained to handle variable image sizes and aspect ratios.
- **Instruct and Reasoning functionalities** with function calls, reasoning effort configurable per request.

Mistral Large 4 offers the following capabilities:

- **Reasoning Mode**: three reasoning efforts — `low`, `medium`, `high` (default) — so the same model can answer a quick chat reply or work through a complex agentic run.
- **Vision**: analyzes images, charts, technical drawings, and documents, with state-of-the-art visual grounding among open weights.
- **Multilingual**: natively fluent in 160+ languages, including all official languages of the European Union.
- **System Prompt**: strong adherence and support for system prompts.
- **Agentic**: native function calling, JSON output, and strict JSON schema enforcement.

releases.body_excerpt:
# Release v5.21.0


## New Model additions

### MiniCPM-OCR

MiniCPM-OCR is a document-understanding model from OpenBMB's MiniCPM-V family. It keeps the MiniCPM-V 4.6 architecture, which pairs a SigLIP vision encoder and a window-attention merger with a Qwen3.5 language model. It is specialized for reading text-dense images such as scanned pages, screenshots, receipts and tables.

**Links:** Documentation | Paper
* Feat test (#49920) by @guarin in #49920

### Flint


Flint is Recursive's mixture-of-experts language model. Compared to a standard SwiGLU MoE transformer such as Qwen3-MoE, it uses hybrid attention (sliding-window attention with rotary embeddings over the current token and the previous 512 tokens in most layers, and full attention without positional encoding in the remaining layers). It also has learned attention sinks, as in GPT-OSS, with per-head RMS-normalized queries and keys. Each sparse layer routes a token to 6 of 256 experts by sigmoid score and adds an ungated shared expert, and the first two layers are dense.

**Links:** Documentation
* Add Flint model support. (#49824) by @lovishmadaan in #49824

### UltraVBert

UltraVBert extends ModernVBert by pairing the UltraBERT text encoder with a SigLIP vision encoder for visual document understanding and retrieval. Its image processor splits each page into 512-pixel tiles plus a global view. The connector merges each 4 x 4 block of vision patches into one token, so a tile becomes 64 image tokens, and RMS-normalizes them to the scale of UltraBERT's token embeddings. The `max_image_tiles` setting (27 by default) caps the number of tiles per page.

**Links:** Documentation
* Add UltraVBERT (#49685) by @athrael-soju in #49685

### Gradium Phonon TTS

Gradium Phonon TTS is Gradium's family of on-device text-to-speech models, trained with the Pocket TTS recipe. A causal transformer reads a voice prompt and the text, then emits one continuous 32-dimensional audio latent per step a

releases.name: tiangolo/fastapi
releases.body_excerpt:
Omitted `bool` and `bool | None` form fields now use their declared defaults or produce missing-field errors, consistent with other fields and Pydantic behavior. FastAPI no longer infers `False` for omitted booleans. This applies to individual form parameters, form models, and unions of form models.

Omitted boolean model fields are excluded from `model_dump(exclude_unset=True)`, and their defaults no longer count as submitted fields during union selection. Default factories and `validate_default` follow the usual rules.

For HTML checkboxes, declare a boolean with a default of `False`. See Boolean Form Fields.

### Breaking Changes

* 🐛 Restore default handling for omitted boolean form fields. PR #16605 by @tiangolo.

releases.name: tiangolo/fastapi
releases.body_excerpt:
Query, header, cookie, and form parameter models now apply their `extra` configuration to all submitted fields in the same parameter location, consistent with Pydantic behavior. This includes fields declared in other models, individual parameters, or dependencies, which were previously excluded.

With `extra="forbid"`, fields outside the model are rejected even if another parameter declares them. With `extra="allow"`, those fields are included as model extras. With the default `extra="ignore"`, they are ignored.

### Breaking Changes

* 🐛 Apply each parameter model's `extra` configuration to sibling fields. PR #16594 by @tiangolo.

### Internal

* ⬆ Bump certifi from 2026.1.4 to 2026.10.19. PR #16571 by [@dependabot[bot]](https://github.com/apps/dependabot).

releases.name: astral-sh/uv
releases.body_excerpt:
## Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-21.

Following uv 0.13.4, which removed the affected eMudhra/emSign root from uv's own certificate store, this release updates the latest managed CPython builds for 3.11 and newer to python-build-standalone 20261021, including the CPython 3.15.1, 3.14.9, and 3.13.17 security patch releases. These builds include pip 26.2.2 both preinstalled in the managed interpreter and bundled with `ensurepip`, which installs pip by default when you run `python -m venv`. Both copies use certifi 2026.10.19, which removes the same affected root. After upgrading uv, run `uv python upgrade` to install the updated builds. Virtual environments pinned to an older Python patch version do not switch to the updated interpreter automatically. Upgrade pip separately in existing virtual environments.

Please note upstream CPython 3.9 and 3.10 still bundle pip releases whose certificate bundles trust the affected eMudhra/emSign root. We recommend migrating off of those versions and will no longer be releasing Docker images with uv installed for EOL Python versions.

### Enhancements

- Report incompatible self-dependencies directly in resolution errors (#21845)

### Python

- Add CPython 3.15.1, 3.14.9, and 3.13.17 (#22802)

### Preview features

- Select and rank wheel variants with no required properties or properties from PEP 850 static providers in platform-specific resolutions with `wheel-variants` (#22535, #22536, #22687, #22688)

### Performance

- Reduce peak memory use when resolving dependencies across multiple environments (#22769, #22770, #22784)
- Speed up exports with complex transitive extras by resolving activation across the dependency graph (#22751)
- Reduce uv's binary size by keeping additional error formatters out of line (#22775)
- Reduce overhead when parsing custom build cache keys (#22749)

### Bug fixes

- Lock packages distributed only as Android wheels without a source distribution (#22806)
- Export optional dependencies correctly

releases.body_excerpt:
This release of DuckDB is named "Cyanoptera" after Spatula Cyanoptera, a species of duck found in western North and South America.

Please also refer to the announcement blog post: https://duckdb.org/2026/10/21/announcing-duckdb-200.html

## What's Changed
* Make `Identifier` a class instead of using string everywhere by @Mytherin in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23161
* Move to tidy-check diff again by @Mytherin in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23196
* Step 3: Make duplicate eliminator optimizer logic work for CTE rewrite by @kryonix in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23187
* Allow `MERGE INTO` in triggers by @Dtenwolde in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23179
* RETURNING support for tables with triggers by @krleonid in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23153
* Remove special formatting code for main CMakeLists.txt by @Mytherin in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23211
* Expand aggregate state export to work with lists (`StateListType`) and sort keys (`StateSortKey`), and add aggregate state export to `list`, `any_value/first/last`, `arg_min/arg_max` by @Mytherin in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23199
* Initial implementation of `variant_array_length` processing function by @sebastiaan-dev in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23167
* Add row group count to parquet RETURN_STATS by @pdet in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23218
* Unify `ProfilerPrintFormat` and `ExplainFormat` , remove special casing and move towards pluggable tree renderers by @Mytherin in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23222
* Rework `quantile` to use `list` infrastructure by @Mytherin in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23228
* Add `decimal_average` aggregate function by @Dtenwolde in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23097
* Step 4: Make unnest rewriter recognize CTE-based plans by @kryonix in https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/23240
* Rework ordered aggregates to use the `list` infrastructure by @Mytherin
